title: US company opens job vacancy for Brazilian Portuguese teacher in the midst.
seoTitle: US Company Seeks Brazilian Portuguese Teacher
subtitle: Ascensus Global seeks specialist to train US military and government officials
excerpt: Ascensus Global announced a vacancy for a Brazilian Portuguese teacher to train US military and intelligence agents, as... increase.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
In recent days, the opening of a vacancy for a Brazilian Portuguese teacher by an American company has drawn the attention of the press and the public. The announcement coincided with the release of a report by the Brazilian Intelligence Agency that raises the possibility of external influence in the 2026 elections to a critical level.

Job vacancy announced by Ascensus Global

Ascensus Global, a service-disabled veteran-owned business, announced on its website the need for a native Brazilian Portuguese professional to conduct a language training program. The candidate will be responsible for teaching classes, conducting interpreting and translation exercises, and participating in other activities aimed at US military and government personnel.

Program format and duration

The training will last three weeks, distributed between October and November. The first week will be held virtually, while the two subsequent weeks will take place in person in Montgomery, Alabama, at Maxwell Air Force Base, the US Air Force's center for Joint Professional Military Education.

Teacher profile and responsibilities

According to the job description, the ideal candidate must have experience teaching languages to military or government professionals, native fluency in Brazilian Portuguese, and familiarity with US military environments. Responsibilities include preparing teaching materials, conducting classes on designated topics, organizing in-person simulations, and evaluating students before and after training.

Context of diplomatic tensions

The job posting comes at a time of rising tensions between Brazil and the United States. At the opening of the 81st UN General Assembly, US President Donald Trump advocated for a more assertive US role in the region, while President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva criticized external interference in electoral processes. The confidential ABIN report, sent to the President of the Republic, the TSE, and the Ministry of Justice, pointed to a trend of escalating US pressure on Brazil.

Relevance to the Brazilian political scenario

The United States' interest in training military and government agents in Brazilian Portuguese reflects a concern with understanding the country's political and cultural reality. The ABIN document warns that US interference could manifest gradually and adaptively, including sanctions and pressure strategies. Although the Brazilian government has not yet officially commented on the report, President Lula expressed his intention to discuss the issue with Trump at the next UN General Assembly.

With information from VEJA, CBN, Gazeta do Povo.
